introduction: Explore New Hope, learn the keep's lore and compare Vitrius's four independent mithral weapon services. Paid crafting is currently unavailable while accounting is active. New discovery and progress require active, ready accounting.
orientation: Vitrius works upstairs at the weaponsmith. ASK vitrius about weapon, shortsword, longsword, two-handed or dagger for his native replies. The troll janitor and centaur visitor discuss Hammerhead and his keep. Listed topics reveal conversation; each keyword is not a separate achievement.

Each weapon service needs one fresh piece of raw mithral, one exact ordinary mithral weapon and its fee: 45 platinum for a shining short sword, 100 for a shining long sword, 250 for a shining two-handed sword, or 10 for a shining dagger. The native recipes are independent. The shining short and long swords are not ingredients for the later recipes.

Raw mithral is placed in a dank prison cell occupied by Zarix and in a maljer hut. Ordinary mithral daggers, short swords and long swords are wielded by the guards of the royal court. Recover the exact chosen ordinary weapon; the shop's black-handled weapons, shining rewards and cracked vault weapons do not substitute. Exact supplied material also fits without a personal kill or source history.

Some of Vitrius's native instructions name a different weapon or omit the dagger. The service cards list the actual accepted ordinary weapon and fee. Carry both materials loose to see current preparation. Held, worn, nested, consumed or handed-away items are not current preparation; ready material does not prove payment or acceptance.

Accounting currently blocks these mixed item-and-coin offerings. The materials can be prepared, but there is no safe payment or crafting completion through this path yet. These are supporting services and award no zone-story achievement or daily credit. Earlier accepted service receipts remain history; owning a shining reward proves no acceptance.

New Hope's village, stables, inn, shops, prison, fields, maljer huts and keep offer exploration and training. The lecherous inn has hidden observation passages and a staircase to its wine cellar. The observer's mirror is descriptive scenery, not a declared travel control. Ordinary shopping, training and exploration do not complete a fifth accepted quest.

ASK janitor about lord, lich, vault, key, dead, keep or hammerhead, and ASK visitor about lord, hammerhead, scout or information. Their account describes Hammerhead's rule and hopes for the village. No accepted request records reporting back to the scout, freeing the prisoners or liberating the village.

Hammerhead carries a petrified heart that fits the locked trapdoor beneath the rug in his bedchamber. SEARCH can reveal hidden exits; UNLOCK and OPEN follow native key and door rules. That route leads down toward the vault. The return trapdoor is hidden and initially closed but unlocked. Exact supplied keys and passages already opened by others remain usable without personal opener history.

The narrow tunnel slopes into water before the tentacler's submerged lair. Follow native movement, breathing, combat and access rules. The solidified eye carried by the tentacler fits the vault entrance, whose lock resists picking. A cracked dagger lying inside fits the return-side lock. The two sides use different keys; opening or unlocking affects a matching reverse door too.

When the tentacler dies, its custom procedure attempts to place one randomly chosen equipment item inside the vault. Its carried eye and wielded lash are separate stock released in the lair by normal removal. Five possible equipment items also have independent reset chances inside the vault; an item already there does not prove the current tentacler death or your own recovery.

The vault's eye can break after use, and the cracked dagger has its own smaller break chance. A successful unlock remains an unlock even if the key breaks. Source caps, chance-based stock, shared doors and recipient resets do not promise a reward or a fresh daily route. Keep access and PvP restrictions in force.

The prisoners, silent observer, illusionist and necromancer add lore and training without accepted rescue or transformation endpoints. The imported mindstone ring has its own guarded travel and protection behavior; it is not a smith ingredient or a local quest receipt. Imported supplies, foreign reuse of village tables and the neighboring hills retain their own ownership and discovery rules.
